description:
As a Software Engineering Teaching Assistant, you will:
Assist the course instructor in preparing teaching materials, including lecture slides, lab guides, coding exercises and assessment content for the software engineering course.
Provide 1-on-1 and group tutoring for students on core software engineering knowledge, covering programming languages, data structures & algorithms, software development lifecycle, version control and software testing.
Grade students' coding assignments, lab reports and projects, and deliver timely, constructive feedback to help students improve their coding skills and academic performance.
Supervise and guide lab sessions, help students troubleshoot technical issues in programming practice, and support students to complete course projects.
Hold regular office hours to answer students' questions about course content, clarify complex technical concepts, and support students' learning progress.
Assist with course administration work, including attendance tracking, course record maintenance, and collecting student feedback to optimize course design.
Maintain an inclusive and positive learning environment, and support students with different learning backgrounds and skill levels.
requiredSkills: Good Academic Performance in Computer Science/Software Engineering Related Courses

description:
As a Lab Support Assistant for the Software Engineering Course Design Intermediate Assessment, you will be responsible for full-process support of the on-site intermediate check activity on April 26, 2026. Your duties include:
Pre-assessment preparation: Assist the instructor to sort out students' course design submission materials, confirm lab equipment, development environment and demo facilities to ensure the smooth progress of the assessment.
On-site assessment support: Verify students' identity and course design completion progress, maintain on-site order of the lab, and guide students to complete the intermediate check process in an orderly manner.
Technical support: Troubleshoot technical problems encountered by students during project demonstration, including code debugging, development environment configuration issues, version control anomalies and demo failures, to ensure students complete the on-site assessment smoothly.
Assessment record management: Assist the instructor to complete on-site assessment records, including students' progress confirmation, problem feedback and signature confirmation, and sort out assessment materials after the activity.
On-site coordination: Cooperate with the instructor to handle unexpected on-site situations, and complete other temporary work related to the intermediate assessment.
requiredSkills: Familiar with Common Development Environments & Version Control Tools
Familiar with Software Engineering Course Design Requirements

description:
As an invigilator for the Software Engineering Test, you will be fully responsible for the standardized invigilation work of the exam, and strictly abide by the school's exam management regulations. Your specific duties are as follows:
Pre-exam preparation: Arrive at the designated exam room TB3-213 in advance to complete pre-exam preparations, including checking and arranging the exam venue, verifying exam equipment, sorting and counting exam papers and answer sheets, and announcing exam discipline and precautions to candidates.
Identity verification: Strictly check the identity documents of candidates before the exam starts, verify the exam eligibility of each candidate, and prevent unqualified personnel from entering the exam room.
On-site invigilation: Maintain strict and fair exam order throughout the exam period, supervise candidates' answering behavior, prevent any form of cheating and discipline violations, and record violations in accordance with regulations.
On-site service & emergency handling: Answer candidates' legitimate questions about exam rules and paper instructions without revealing exam-related answers; promptly and properly handle on-site emergencies such as physical discomfort of candidates, paper damage, and equipment failures in accordance with the school's exam management specifications.
Post-exam work: Accurately collect, count and check all exam papers and answer sheets after the exam ends, ensure that the number of collected papers matches the number of candidates, seal the exam papers as required, and complete the exam record filing and venue finishing work.
Complete other temporary invigilation-related work assigned by the course instructor and exam management department.
